canonical_definition: Safety in AI systems refers to the capability to avoid generating harmful, toxic, or adversarial outputs while handling sensitive content appropriately, often operationalized through resistance to jailbreaking attacks, preference for refusal responses to unsafe requests, and detoxification of harmful content. Some definitions emphasize truthfulness, ethical judgment, and balanced caution to avoid overcautious refusals, though variations exist in whether safety is explicitly optimized or considered secondary to other objectives. Disagreements arise in prioritizing resistance to adversarial prompts versus mitigating over-alignment effects that may suppress benign responses.
